## Food experiences on a Bolivia–Brazil–Chile–Peru journey

Bolivia, Brazil, Chile and Peru can be visited as part of a [six-country Latin American tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/). The complete itinerary also goes through Argentina and Uruguay. The four-country filter does not represent a separate journey that omits those two countries.

For food-loving travelers, one detail is crucial: **a specific wine tasting is offered during the Chilean stage as an optional paid excursion**. The main trip focuses on cities, Iguazu Falls, Bolivia's highlands and Peruvian landmarks. It cannot be described as a continuous series of cooking classes and tastings in all four countries.

## Chile: the Maipo Valley and an optional winery trip

On the day of the [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) city tour, an additional paid excursion to the wineries of the [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) with wine tasting is offered. This is the program's most clearly defined food-and-wine activity.

Why decide in advance? The schedule includes city sightseeing followed by a flight to Calama and a transfer to San Pedro de Atacama. Adding wineries means agreeing on the duration, transport and compatibility with the main excursions. The mere appearance of Maipo Valley among possible excursions does not confirm that a tasting is included.

If wine is your primary motivation, compare this itinerary with [Chile's food-and-wine tours](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/chile/). The wine component takes up only a limited part of the full route.

## Brazil: Rio and Iguazu without a dedicated food program

The Brazil stage combines [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). In Rio, the itinerary includes Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain and a city tour. At Iguazu, the emphasis is on the waterfalls.

Brazilian cuisine is diverse, but that does not mean this particular tour includes a tasting, a restaurant-based food tour or a cooking lesson. Travelers who want to add a themed dinner or market visit should discuss it as a change to the itinerary, separate from the confirmed services.

## Bolivia: meals during a high-altitude journey

From Chile's San Pedro de Atacama, travelers embark on a two-day 4x4 route through Bolivian lagoons to [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The program includes an overnight stay at an expedition-style desert hotel. Meals are provided on parts of the journey, including a packed lunch.

This matters for travel logistics, but **an ordinary included lunch is not a food-focused excursion**. Altitudes above 4,000 meters, long drives and expedition-style meals limit opportunities for impromptu lengthy restaurant stops. The central experience here is the high-altitude landscape, not a tasting program.

## Peru: Cusco and Machu Picchu without a promised culinary tour

The Peru stage travels via Puno to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), then to Lima. Historical and sightseeing excursions are included. Restaurant visits, Peruvian cooking classes or specialized tastings as independent products are not specified in the verified program.

Peru has much to offer national-cuisine enthusiasts, but when choosing this particular tour, distinguish between the opportunity to try local dishes while traveling and a prepaid food-focused event. If cuisine is your main interest, compare [food-and-wine routes through Peru](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/peru/).

## Making a wine experience a meaningful part of the extended trip

For this combination, the choice is between a broad sightseeing journey and one where food and wine are the primary purpose. In the first case, the optional Maipo wineries enhance a busy itinerary around South America. In the second, it makes sense to choose the desired tastings and regions first and build dates and logistics around them, rather than assuming food experiences are included in every country.

We can discuss which additional visits fit the selected sequence of cities, flights and high-altitude drives. The availability, price and feasibility of a specific service are confirmed separately; it does not automatically become part of the original tour price.

The trip components, accommodation, included services and dates are detailed in the [current six-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/). Other combinations can be found in the [multi-country food-and-wine catalog](/multi-country/interests/food-and-wine/) and the [general Bolivia, Brazil, Chile and Peru selection](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_chile_peru/).

## Frequently asked questions about food and wine

### Is the Maipo Valley wine tasting included in the tour price?

No. The Chilean winery excursion and tasting is listed as an optional activity at additional cost.

### Are food-focused excursions included in all four countries?

No. The confirmed themed experience concerns the Maipo Valley. The other stages focus mainly on natural attractions, history and general sightseeing.

### Can we add more tastings?

An additional program can be discussed separately, taking flights, transfers and main sightseeing days into account. Discussing an option does not guarantee the availability or inclusion of any particular service.

buttonLabel: "Explore nature in Bolivia, Brazil, Chile and Peru"
lead: >-
  Bolivia, Brazil, Chile and Peru on one journey reveal a remarkable contrast between tropical forests, the ocean coast and the Andes' high-altitude deserts. In Brazil, the routes link Rio de Janeiro with Iguazu; in Chile they reach Atacama; in Bolivia they cross lagoons and the Uyuni Salt Flat; in Peru they continue via Titicaca toward Machu Picchu. These nature experiences belong to extended trips through five or more countries, so comparing actual stops and travel demands is essential.
---

## From Brazil's humid forests to Bolivia's salt flats

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} in which [Bolivia](/bolivia/), [Brazil](/brazil/), [Chile](/chile/) and [Peru](/peru/) are principal destinations and nature experiences form a substantial part of the journey. These are not tours confined to exactly four countries: the itineraries also include Argentina, and some include Uruguay, Ecuador and Colombia.

The natural contrasts are striking. Brazil brings water and humid forests; Chile dry highlands; Bolivia mineral-rich lagoons and broad salt plains; Peru a vast lake and mountain valleys. Unlike a journey within one climate zone, this trip requires frequent changes of clothing and travel conditions.

## Brazil: Rio and Iguazu Falls

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the routes begin beside the Atlantic Ocean. Views from [Sugarloaf Mountain](/brazil/place/sugarloaf-mountain/) reveal how granite peaks, bays and urban neighborhoods meet. Some itineraries also mention [Tijuca National Park](/brazil/place/tijuca-national-park/), where stretches of Atlantic Forest survive within the city.

The main natural attraction in Brazil on these tours is [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The cascades are surrounded by humid subtropical forest; powerful water flow generates clouds of spray, and visitors can view the system from established walkways. The falls extend across the border to [Puerto Iguazú in Argentina](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). Both national parks have natural heritage recognized by UNESCO. Itineraries including both sides need separate time for the border crossing.

Importantly, a “Nature” category does not establish that an extra Tijuca hike in Rio or a special wildlife photography outing at Iguazu is included. Check each tour's actual excursions.

## Chile: dry climate and the journey across Atacama

The Chilean stage passes through [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) and nearby desert regions. After humid Rio and Iguazu, the landscape changes sharply: sparse vegetation, strong high-altitude sunshine, dry mountain expanses and long distances between settlements.

San Pedro matters not only as a destination but also as the starting point for the crossing into Bolivia. Road journeys take time because of altitude and conditions. An “Atacama” entry in the itinerary does not automatically include every individual attraction, such as the [Valley of the Moon](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/), [Atacama Salt Flat](/chile/place/atacama-salt-flat/) or geysers. Expect those places only when they appear explicitly in the program.

## Bolivia: geothermal fields and Uyuni

The journey continues through [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and the [Sol de Mañana geysers](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/) toward [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Mountain lakes, steaming geothermal zones and the salt plain form a series of different nature stops, not one location under several names.

Laguna Colorada stands out for its water color, although the exact shade varies with lighting and the lake's natural conditions. In dry weather, Uyuni displays its salt surface and characteristic patterns; with a shallow layer of water, it can reflect the sky. Neither intense lake color nor the mirror effect can be promised as an unchanging feature.

Compared with Brazil, the Bolivia section is at a much higher elevation and calls for a different pace. Distances between stops, unpaved-road conditions, overnight accommodation and protection from cold are especially important. Difficulty should not be judged by map distance alone.

## Peru: a high-altitude lake and green mountain slopes

The nature route in Peru continues through [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). After Bolivia's dry high plateau, the broad expanse of water changes the landscape completely. A visit to the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/) adds human history to this natural attraction; it is a lake excursion, not a stand-alone safari.

Near [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), the journey continues to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Mountain slopes become greener and the archaeological site sits within a deep valley. UNESCO recognizes both the cultural and natural qualities of this historic sanctuary. For travelers, distinguish a conventional visit to the ruins from a separate multi-day mountain trek: the latter cannot be assumed to be included.

## Choosing the right level of intensity

| Natural contrast | Where to experience it |
|---|---|
| Ocean and mountains within a city | Rio de Janeiro |
| Humid forest and waterfalls | Iguazu |
| Dry mountain desert | Atacama |
| Colorful lagoons | Bolivian highlands |
| Salt plain | Uyuni |
| Lake among the Andes | Titicaca |
| Green slopes and the Incas | Machu Picchu |

Compare the [18-day five-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/), [20-day six-country option](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and [32-day journey](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Longer itineraries cover more territory, but that does not necessarily mean more time at each natural attraction. Choose based on individual excursions and the number of transfers.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki,tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026,tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

If you want routes without a thematic filter, see the [Bolivia, Brazil, Chile and Peru combination](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_chile_peru/). For more nature destinations, browse the [full multi-country nature selection](/multi-country/interests/nature/).

## Frequently asked questions about nature in these four countries

### Do the programs include an Amazon rainforest expedition?

Our routes feature Rio, Iguazu, Atacama, Bolivia and Peru. **Including Brazil in a filter does not imply a separate Amazon expedition.** If the Amazon is your goal, select a tour that explicitly includes it as a stage.

### Can we see both sides of Iguazu Falls?

Current programs feature both [Foz do Iguaçu in Brazil](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and [Puerto Iguazú in Argentina](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). Check the day's actual activities and border logistics on your chosen tour.

### How does Uyuni differ from the Atacama Desert?

[Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) is best known for its salt surface, while [Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) encompasses Chile's dry desert and mountain regions. They occupy different stages of the extended route and offer different types of terrain.

### Where is the most noticeable change of climate?

When moving from humid parts of Brazil to the dry, cold high-altitude areas of Chile and Bolivia. This affects shoes, clothes and how travelers feel during transfers.

### Will there be a separate mountain trek in Peru?

The inclusion of [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) alone does not establish that. Visiting the archaeological site and completing a multi-day hiking route are different formats.

## Where to look for wildlife on a four-country route

The principal nature experiences take place at [Iguazu Falls in Brazil](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and on Bolivia's Altiplano. At Iguazu, the route follows paths through humid forest and waterfalls; in Bolivia, travelers take 4x4 vehicles to lakes frequented by flamingos. Chile connects these landscapes via the Atacama Desert. The Peru section visits Titicaca and ancient Inca cities, but in the featured itineraries it focuses on culture, not dedicated wildlife observation.

Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. This is a four-country intersection, not a self-contained itinerary limited to these nations. For comparison, we also refer below to [nature routes through these four countries](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_chile_peru/interests/nature/), including an [18-day five-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) that visits Argentina. Their main nature theme is scenery; a stop at a lagoon with birds does not automatically make them specialist wildlife tours. Compare the full country and day sequence rather than relying only on the filter name.

## Brazil: waterfalls and humid tropical forest

The Brazil portions of these tours begin in Rio de Janeiro and continue to Iguazu. Established walkways in the national park provide views of powerful waterfalls against dense greenery. This is chiefly a nature excursion to the cascades, not an organized safari: sightings of wild animals are not promised.

[Parque das Aves at Iguazu](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/) is offered as an optional excursion in some programs. Distinguish it from the included walk to the falls: before selecting a tour, check whether the bird park visit is provided and under which conditions. If Brazilian nature is your main goal, compare [Brazilian nature tours](/interests/nature/tours/brazil/), which may allow more time within one ecosystem.

## Chile and Bolivia: from Atacama to the Altiplano's flamingos

After Santiago, the itineraries lead to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The Chilean section features volcanoes, desert expanses and a transition from the big city to dry highlands. Visiting Atacama alone does not mean a specialist birdwatching excursion is included.

The Bolivian 4x4 section then begins. The programs explicitly name [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) with James's flamingos and a chain of high-altitude lakes, including [Laguna Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/). This is the most concrete birdwatching episode on the journey. These birds live in the wild, so neither their number nor how close they will be can be predicted.

Much of the Bolivia section takes place above 4,000 meters. Clothing for cold wind, sun protection and sufficient time to adapt are essential. The [20-day six-country program](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) provides expedition-style accommodation at high altitude. Travelers who struggle with elevation and long drives in 4x4 vehicles should discuss the pace before booking.

## Peru: Titicaca, Cusco and a different purpose

The route from Bolivia into Peru leads to [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), then Cusco and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). It includes a boat trip to the Uros Islands, an introduction to the Andean region and visits to historical sites. These days do not become dedicated wildlife-watching excursions.

If encounters with wild animals are essential to the trip, discuss a different selection of destinations and additional days. [Wildlife-watching tours in Peru](/interests/wildlife/tours/peru/) offer alternatives to compare, but each route must be assessed by its advertised activities, not merely its category.

## Which current itinerary should you choose?

The [18-day five-country group tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) suits those wanting Iguazu, Bolivian lagoons and Machu Picchu while accepting frequent flights and road journeys. [Six countries in 20 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) add Uruguay and city excursions: wildlife observation occupies only part of the trip. The [32-day eight-country route](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) continues to Ecuador and Colombia and requires much more time. It includes separate sea excursions to observe wildlife in the Galápagos, but those belong to the Ecuador stage and do not imply wildlife watching in all four countries of this selection.

Some routes are tied to festivals. The [five-country New Year trip](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) begins with celebrations on Copacabana, while the [Rio Champions' Parade tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) is tied to Carnival. For flamingo watching, these schedules mean lagoon visits are determined by the calendar of the wider journey.

When choosing, compare three things: time in natural areas, nights spent at altitude, and which visits are included or optional. We help coordinate country order, flights and ground transfers so a packed itinerary still allows time at its most interesting destinations.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Bolivia, Brazil, Chile and Peru

### Where can we actually observe flamingos on these programs?

At high-altitude lagoons in Bolivia, particularly Laguna Colorada. The itineraries travel through the region by 4x4, but the number of birds and their distance cannot be guaranteed.

### Can we see animals in each of the four countries?

This is not an objective of the featured itineraries. Bolivia offers a confirmed flamingo encounter, while Brazil offers waterfall walks through tropical forest. Chile and Peru mainly reveal scenery and cultural sites on these routes.

### What is the hardest part of combining Iguazu and the Bolivian lagoons?

The abrupt change from a warm, humid waterfall region to dry, cold highlands. Alongside appropriate clothing, travelers need a reasonable pace and sufficient time for road transfers.

### Is this suitable as a dedicated birdwatching trip?

It is a multi-theme journey. If birds are the main goal, first confirm the duration of stops at the lagoons and whether specialist observation excursions are included; they may be absent from the basic program.

## Bolivia, Brazil, Chile and Uruguay: how the four countries connect

These destinations show different sides of South America. [Brazil](/brazil/) offers [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and Iguazu Falls; [Uruguay](/uruguay/) provides a walk through [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) on the opposite bank of the Río de la Plata; [Chile](/chile/) brings Santiago and [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). In [Bolivia](/bolivia/), the route follows high mountain roads between lagoons and salt flats toward [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/).

Our catalog has {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that include all four as principal countries: the [20-day six-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and the [32-day eight-country tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Both begin in Brazil, continue via Argentina and Uruguay into Chile and Bolivia, then Peru. The second journey extends beyond Peru into Ecuador and Colombia.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026,tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

**The four selected countries do not form a separate four-country itinerary.** When choosing a trip, consider every country through which the flights, excursions and overland transfers actually pass.

## Rio, both sides of Iguazu and the road to Argentina

The Brazil section includes excursions to Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain and around the city. A flight to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) follows. The falls are visited from the Brazilian and then the Argentine side, via [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/).

Moving between the two sides of the falls is an international border crossing with passport control. The time needed at the parks cannot be estimated from the distance between viewing points: border procedures, transfers, tickets and access to park paths all matter. Optional boat excursions and the Bird Park must be checked separately against the specific tour conditions.

After Iguazu, the itinerary goes to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) for city excursions. Neither of these offers provides a direct route from Rio or Iguazu to Bolivia's salt flat.

## Uruguay: a sightseeing day, not a separate holiday

Travelers take a ferry from Buenos Aires to Montevideo. The itinerary includes exploring the city and returning to Argentina. This is an interesting way to compare the two capitals: Buenos Aires' architecture and streets against downtown Montevideo and its waterfronts.

But **the Uruguay stage lasts just one day**. A resort-coast holiday and several nights in Uruguay are not included in either tour. More time in the country would require changing dates, accommodation and subsequent flights.

The ferry excursion entails leaving Argentina and entering it again. Plan documentation for both border crossings on the same day and allow time to check in for the return sailing. After the return, the route continues with a flight from Buenos Aires to [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/).

## Chile: from Santiago to Atacama

A city tour is planned in Santiago. Travelers then fly to Calama and transfer to San Pedro de Atacama, where the overland journey toward Bolivia begins. Here, the change from major capitals to dry desert and high-altitude terrain is especially noticeable.

The Chilean portion of these tours focuses on **central and northern Chile**. Patagonia, Torres del Paine and southern glaciers are not included. Travelers interested in those natural parks need a different Chile–Argentina program.

The border crossing around Hito Cajón is at high altitude. Access, opening hours and vehicle requirements should be checked before traveling. The ready-made programs use 4x4 vehicles. An ordinary urban transfer is not an equivalent substitute for this journey.

## Bolivia: lagoons, Uyuni and La Paz

After the Chilean border, the 4x4 route passes [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), high-altitude lagoons and geothermal areas before reaching the salt landscapes around [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). This multi-day section is strongly affected by transport, overnight arrangements and weather.

The salt flat looks different depending on season. Water on the surface can create reflections, but it can also restrict access to parts of the route. A travel date cannot guarantee both a perfect mirror effect and free vehicle access to every viewpoint.

After Uyuni comes a flight to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), a city tour and a visit to [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/). The journey then crosses the Bolivia–Peru border toward Lake Titicaca. The Bolivian days are both a substantial experience in their own right and the connection to Peru.

## Altitude, climate and packing: different conditions in one journey

Humidity in Rio and Iguazu contrasts sharply with Atacama and Bolivia's Altiplano. The desert can be sunny during the day, while highland areas can be windy and cold, especially early in the morning and overnight. Walks through Buenos Aires and Montevideo call for another clothing combination.

| Stage | What to consider |
|---|---|
| Rio and Iguazu | Humidity, rain, lightweight clothing |
| Montevideo | Waterfront wind, walking |
| Santiago and Atacama | Dry air, sun exposure |
| Highland Bolivia | Cold, altitude, remote roads |

Bring layered clothing, closed shoes and protection from wind, sun and rain. Check baggage sizes for internal flights, as airline rules may differ.

**The high-altitude section requires an individual assessment of fitness and health.** Altitude sickness can affect physically fit travelers too. Discuss personal risks with a doctor and confirm medical insurance coverage for the altitudes and overland activities planned.

## Borders, currencies and money on the road

The four selected countries use the boliviano (BOB), Brazilian real (BRL), Chilean peso (CLP) and Uruguayan peso (UYU). The actual itineraries also involve spending in Argentina, which uses the peso (ARS), and Peru, which uses the sol (PEN). Ecuador and Colombia are added on the eight-country route.

It is particularly useful to plan cash for personal purchases before entering remote highland regions, where ATMs and exchange offices may be scarce. Check international card acceptance with the issuer. Visa and Mastercard cards issued by Russian banks do not work abroad through those networks.

Border requirements must be checked by nationality for the full route: Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Peru, plus Ecuador and Colombia if you choose the longer option. Re-entry to Argentina after Montevideo and the crossings among Chile, Bolivia and Peru deserve particular attention.

## What 20-day and 32-day itineraries offer

Both tours include Rio, Iguazu, Buenos Aires, Montevideo, Santiago, Atacama, Uyuni, La Paz and Peruvian sights. The 20-day route ends in Lima. The 32-day itinerary continues through Ecuador, including the Galápagos, and then Colombia.

The additional 12 days are not 12 days on Uruguayan beaches or in Bolivia. They extend the journey beyond Peru. Compare the day sequence, number of flights and confirmed included services, not simply the total duration.

## Frequently asked questions about Bolivia, Brazil, Chile and Uruguay

### Can we travel straight from Brazil to Bolivia on a ready-made itinerary?

No. Current programs pass through Argentina, Uruguay and Chile between them. A customized selection of countries would need separate planning.

### Is the Uruguay portion a beach holiday?

No. Montevideo is visited on a one-day ferry excursion from Buenos Aires.

### Is Chilean Patagonia included?

No. The Chilean stage covers Santiago, Calama and San Pedro de Atacama before the 4x4 journey into Bolivia.

### Which stage is the most challenging in terms of transport?

The high-altitude Atacama–Bolivia section, where 4x4 vehicles are used and the border crossing requires coordinated timing and documents.

### Which personal expenses should be prepared in advance?

Cash for purchases in remote parts of Bolivia, optional excursions and expenses excluded from the particular tour. The paid-for services are listed on each product page.

## Where the real adventure starts on the route

Routes that include [Bolivia](/bolivia/), [Brazil](/brazil/), [Chile](/chile/) and [Uruguay](/uruguay/) change dramatically as the journey progresses. Rio and Montevideo are mainly about city sightseeing, Iguazu brings walks through nature, and the most demanding section begins after San Pedro de Atacama: an overland 4x4 route through Bolivia's highlands.

Our selection features [Six Latin American Countries in 20 Days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and [Eight South American Countries in 32 Days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Both include the four selected countries but also necessarily visit Argentina and Peru. The longer journey continues through Ecuador and Colombia. **These are two extensive itineraries, not an isolated trip through only four countries.**

## Brazil: nature routes at Iguazu

Both itineraries begin with [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), including Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain and city sightseeing. Travelers then fly toward [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), where the focus shifts from urban experiences to nature.

The itinerary includes a visit to the Brazilian side of the falls. Some program versions also mention separate excursion modules for the Bird Park and the Macuco Safari boat route. Their exact status, participation conditions and restrictions must be checked in the chosen program: the presence of a stand-alone excursion does not mean every optional water activity is equally available to all participants.

Travelers then visit the Argentine side of Iguazu via [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). Border control and walking in both parks take additional time. A buffer is especially important if optional water activities are planned or certain trails are temporarily unavailable.

## Uruguay: a short city stage between natural regions

[Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is visited from Buenos Aires on a one-day ferry excursion. Visitors can explore another capital's architecture and waterfront, but these published itineraries do not include multi-day hiking, rafting or an independent sporting adventure in Uruguay.

Uruguay is best viewed as a cultural pause before the more demanding high-altitude days. The ferry means leaving Argentina and returning to it: check passport rules, boarding times and re-entry requirements for the particular nationality and date. The journey then continues with a flight to [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/).

## Chile: San Pedro de Atacama as the gateway to the Altiplano

After city sightseeing in Santiago, travelers fly to Calama and transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The stop matters for preparing for higher elevations: daytime and nighttime conditions differ sharply in the region, and the subsequent roads rise far above urban areas.

The programs include a separate evening astronomy excursion in Atacama. This is another type of experience, but the main adventure demands begin later, at the Bolivian crossing. Chilean Patagonia and extended Torres del Paine treks are **not included** in these two itineraries; anyone particularly interested in Patagonian hiking should explore [Chile tours](/chile/tour/) with different geography.

The Hito Cajón border complex near San Pedro stands at approximately 4,550 meters. Check border operating hours and permitted transport before the trip. This is not a short city transfer: altitude, wind, road conditions and passport control genuinely affect the whole day.

## Bolivia: 4x4 vehicles, colorful lagoons and the salt flat

The main active stage runs through Bolivia's highlands in 4x4 vehicles. The [32-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) includes a two-day jeep route with an English-speaking guide. The [20-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) also has a dedicated 4x4 section through Bolivia's lagoons and salt flats.

The sights include [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), the Salvador Dalí Desert, geothermal areas, [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and other high-altitude lagoons. The route then follows salt flats and reaches [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). What matters here is not just the scenery but also long drives, remote stops, possible weather restrictions and adherence to a planned route.

Uyuni looks different in wet and dry seasons. Reflections on a water-covered surface cannot be guaranteed for any date, and excess water can change access to certain areas. Choose the season according to your main goal and discuss alternatives with the organizer rather than expecting both a perfect mirror and unrestricted 4x4 driving everywhere.

After the high-altitude stage, the itinerary includes a flight to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), then a visit to historic [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) and onward travel to Peru. The 4x4 crossing days remain the most active part, rather than the ordinary La Paz city excursion.

## Altitude, well-being and equipment

For many travelers, the biggest challenge is **moving quickly from low-lying cities to areas thousands of meters above sea level**. Fitness alone does not protect against altitude sickness. CDC guidance stresses gradual acclimatization and assessment of individual medical risks. Discuss your health with a doctor ahead of time and check whether your medical insurance covers the stated altitudes and types of activity.

Bring comfortable closed shoes, warm layered clothing, wind protection, sunglasses and rain protection. Humid Brazil, city stops and the cold Altiplano require different items. Preparation should also account for baggage limits on domestic flights and the amount of luggage that will actually fit in the vehicle during the 4x4 portion.

Transfers and documents must be coordinated for the complete route, including Argentina, Peru and, on the longer version, Ecuador and Colombia. Ada Tours helps arrange flights and transfers in sequence, check nationality-specific border requirements and agree on the pace. Choose the itinerary and included services from the specific tour, without assuming identical conditions for every country and date.

## Frequently asked questions about adventures in Bolivia, Brazil, Chile and Uruguay

### Which is the hardest stage of the two programs?

The high-altitude crossing from Chile's Atacama into Bolivia, with 4x4 days, lagoons and the Uyuni Salt Flat. It requires more attention to elevation and weather than sightseeing in Rio or Montevideo.

### Is a Patagonia trek included?

No. Both programs travel through Santiago and Atacama in northern Chile. A different itinerary is needed for hiking in Patagonia.

### Is specialist mountaineering equipment necessary?

Bolivia's main section uses 4x4 transport rather than technical climbing. Warm clothing, closed shoes and high-altitude preparation are nevertheless necessary. Equipment and medical restrictions depend on any additional activities selected.

### Can the journey be shortened to four countries?

This selection does not offer a ready-made stand-alone four-country product. Both current itineraries also include Argentina and Peru. A customized route would require revisiting borders, flights, dates and included services.
